name: Vakanssi: Careers Page, Hiring & Applicant Tracking
author: Vakanssi

sections.description:
Vakanssi is a complete applicant tracking system (ATS) for WordPress: branded job listings with Google-for-Jobs
structured data, a native application form, an applications inbox with a configurable drag-and-drop
pipeline board, templated emails, and tools for handling candidate data (export, erasure and
scheduled retention), all on your own server, with no per-seat SaaS fees.

A complete hiring workflow:

  • Jobs & careers: a vakanssi_job post type, a branded careers archive (at /jobs/ by default, or on
    your own careers page) and [vakanssi_jobs] shortcode, and valid Google-for-Jobs JobPosting structured data that is
    withheld automatically when a job is not eligible (expired, no location, no apply path, …).
  • Application intake: a native application form with a secure CV upload (type-verified by magic
    bytes, randomised filename, owner-only permissions), spam/honeypot/rate-limiting, and candidate
    de-duplication by email.
  • Applications inbox & pipeline board: a sortable, filterable inbox plus a build-free React
    Kanban board with a candidate profile drawer; configurable stages; bulk move/delete.
  • Interviews & calendar invites: schedule an interview from the candidate’s record and send a
    real .ics invite that Google, Outlook and Apple render as an actionable event, with no OAuth and
    no connected account. Reschedule, cancel, and keep internal notes that reach your interviewers’
    calendars and never the candidate’s.
  • Application data & export: export applications to CSV, print or save any application as a PDF, and edit application details, right from the inbox.
  • Email: templated confirmation/recruiter/rejection/offer emails with personalization tags and
    an SMTP-compatible sender, logged and de-duplicated.
  • Candidate data controls: consent capture, WordPress core data export/erase integration (with a
    complete cascade across all candidate data), a retention-purge cron, and an audit log. These are
    tools you operate; they do not by themselves make a site compliant with any particular law.
  • Blocks, page builders & themes: a Job Listings block for the block editor, native Elementor
    widgets for the listing, the application form and the job details (Elementor Pro Theme Builder
    archive/single templates are respected too), a Divi module, and shortcodes for everywhere else.
    Block themes on WordPress 6.7 and later get editable Site Editor templates; classic themes get the
    built-in archive.
  • First-run setup wizard: sender identity and a careers page in a few clicks, with optional
    sample content and a prompt to post your first job.
  • Foundations: scale-ready custom tables (engineered for 10k+ applications), a modular
    architecture (disabled modules load no code/assets), capability-based roles (Recruiter, Hiring
    Manager, HR/Compliance), and a vakanssi/v1 REST API with per-route
    permission checks.

External services

Vakanssi does not contact any external service on its own. Everything it stores stays on
your server. One optional integration talks to a third party, and only after you switch it
on and enter your own credentials:

Cloudflare Turnstile (optional spam protection for the public application form)

Turnstile is off by default. It activates only once you enter a Turnstile site key and
secret under Hiring → Settings → Application form. While it is enabled:

  • each visitor’s browser loads the challenge script from
    https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js;
  • when someone submits an application, the resulting challenge token, the visitor’s IP
    address and your secret key are sent to
    https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify so Cloudflare can confirm the
    submission is not automated;
  • when an administrator uses “Test these keys” on the settings screen, that admin’s browser
    loads the same challenge script, and the resulting token, the admin’s IP address and the
    secret key being tested are sent to the same address, so the key pair can be checked
    without waiting for a real application.

No application content (no name, email, CV, or answers) is sent to Cloudflare. Turning the
setting off stops all contact with the service.

Service: https://www.cloudflare.com/products/turnstile/
Terms of service: https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/
Privacy policy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the vakanssi folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install through the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin. Activation creates the database tables, installs roles, provisions protected
    file storage, and opens a short setup wizard.
  3. Complete Hiring → Setup (sender email, careers page), post your first job, then review
    Hiring → Tools → Status for system status.
sections.faq:
Does removing the plugin delete my candidate data?

No. Uninstalling removes roles, capabilities, and plugin settings, but your hiring data is kept
unless you explicitly enable Hiring → Settings → General → Delete all data on uninstall.
While another copy of Vakanssi is still installed (for example in a second plugin folder),
deleting a copy removes nothing, so the copy you keep runs with its settings and data.

Are uploaded CVs protected from direct download?

Yes, with defence in depth. Candidate files are stored in a protected vakanssi folder in
your uploads directory, under random 128-bit file names, with an Apache deny rule, index guards and a
generated Nginx rule. Vakanssi then verifies over HTTP that the folder is not directly reachable,
and shows an admin warning (with the exact Nginx rule to add) if it is. The plugin itself only serves
CVs through an authenticated, permission-checked download link.
To keep them outside your public site entirely, define VAKANSSI_STORAGE_DIR as an absolute path in wp-config.php; moving your existing CVs is covered at https://docs.vakanssi.com/admin/move-cv-storage/

Who on my team can see candidate applications and CVs?

Anyone you grant a hiring role to. Vakanssi ships three roles (Recruiter, Hiring Manager, and HR / Compliance)
plus Administrator, and any user with the “view applications” capability can see every candidate
and download every CV in the pipeline. In other words, Vakanssi does not restrict staff to only
the jobs or candidates assigned to them: it assumes your hiring team is trusted, which is the right
default for most small teams. Only grant these roles to people who should see all applicants.

How do I report a security issue?

Email security@vakanssi.com rather than posting in the support forum, so a fix can ship before
the details are public. Please include the Vakanssi version, your WordPress and PHP versions, and
steps to reproduce. You will get an acknowledgement within three business days and an initial
assessment within a week, and you will be credited in the changelog for the release that fixes it
unless you would rather not be. Only the most recent release receives security fixes, so updating
is always part of the answer.

What personal data is included in a GDPR data-export request?

When you run Tools → Export Personal Data for a candidate’s email, Vakanssi includes their
profile (name, email, phone, location), every application (position, stage, status, date, and whether
consent was given), the cover letter, their LinkedIn profile, each uploaded CV/attachment (the file itself, with its
filename and upload date), the submission context stored with the application (the page the application was sent from), the
recruiter notes and interview notes written about them, their interviews, and the emails Vakanssi
sent them. Other details stored with an application or the candidate are included too, under
“Additional application data”. The export deliberately does not name the staff member who wrote a note, gave a
rating, or conducted an interview. That is a third party’s personal data, not the candidate’s.

The matching Erase Personal Data tool removes all of it, including the CV files on disk. Export
and erasure share one list of the tables that hold notes, interviews and emails about a candidate,
so the two stay in step.

Does it work on WordPress multisite?

Yes, activated per site or network-wide. Each site keeps its own jobs, candidates, CVs and
settings (data is never shared between sites), and each site chooses independently whether
deleting the plugin also deletes its hiring data. There is no network-level configuration screen; settings are per site.

Network activation is the recommended setup: deleting a site then removes that site’s Vakanssi
data with it, and if some of its CVs cannot be deleted, Vakanssi keeps the list of those files.
With per-site activation, a site deleted where Vakanssi is not active keeps its Vakanssi tables,
and its CVs when they are in a custom storage folder. Since 1.3.0 a super admin sees this data in
Site Health and under Hiring → Tools → Data, and removes it there after a confirmation. When
Vakanssi cannot prove a site’s CV files are gone (for example a folder it cannot read), it keeps
that site’s file list and says why. A single site turned into a network keeps finding the CVs it
stored before, and Site Health names the folder to move them from.

Does it work on Nginx?

Yes. Nginx ignores .htaccess, so add the generated location block to your server config. The
plugin’s screens show the rule, and Site Health flags the folder, when it is reachable.

Does it work with my theme and page builder?

Yes, and you do not have to fall back to a shortcode. The block editor gets a Job Listings
block. Elementor gets three native widgets (the listing, the application form, and the job
details) grouped under a Vakanssi section in the panel, and they work with the free Elementor; if
you run Elementor Pro, your Theme Builder archive and single templates for jobs are used instead of
ours. Divi gets a Jobs module. Shortcodes ([vakanssi_jobs], [vakanssi_job_apply],
[vakanssi_job_details]) still work anywhere else, including builders with no dedicated
integration.

Themes need nothing special. Block themes on WordPress 6.7 and later get editable “Jobs archive” (while the archive page is on)
and “Single job” templates in the Site Editor, built from your own header and footer; classic themes get the built-in archive. The
candidate-facing pages are styled so they survive a theme’s own CSS reset, so the listing and the
apply button look the same whichever theme you run.

Can I restyle the careers/job pages, and will custom CSS slow my site down?

Yes. Under Hiring → Settings → Jobs & Careers → Appearance you can turn off Vakanssi’s front-end stylesheet
entirely, if your theme styles the markup. For your own styling, use WordPress’s built-in editor at
Appearance → Customize → Additional CSS, which adds no extra request. Vakanssi keeps its own
selectors deliberately low-weight and its class names stable. Match their weight, such as
.vakanssi-apply-form .vakanssi-apply-button for the application form’s Submit button or
.vakanssi-apply .vakanssi-apply-button for a job’s Apply link, and style :hover, :focus and
:active as well, since Vakanssi sets those too. On most pages that is enough without !important.

The same vakanssi- class names are on the careers and job pages under block themes and classic
themes alike, so one rule covers both. On a block theme your theme keeps control of the page width
and spacing and Vakanssi adds no styling of its own to those wrappers, so your rules apply exactly
as you write them.

Do I need any special server setup for a production site?

Two things are worth doing on a live hiring site, and both are standard WordPress production
hygiene rather than Vakanssi requirements. First, switch WordPress to a real cron trigger:
out of the box, WordPress runs scheduled tasks only when someone visits your site, so on a
quiet careers site scheduled work can run late. Vakanssi relies on it to purge candidate data once
its retention period is up. Add define( 'DISABLE_WP_CRON', true ); to wp-config.php and trigger
wp-cron.php every few minutes; most managed hosts offer this as a checkbox. Second, if your
host offers a persistent object cache (Redis or Memcached), enable it: Vakanssi uses
transients for its dashboard counters, and an object cache keeps those out of the database
under heavy traffic. Apply-form rate limits always use the database, so they hold either way. Nothing breaks without either step.

Can I disable the /jobs/ archive page?

Yes: Hiring → Settings → Jobs & Careers → Job URLs → “Archive page”. Single job pages stay
live under your job URL base (e.g. /jobs/job-title/); the archive URL becomes available for your own
page, such as a Careers page using the [vakanssi_jobs] shortcode.

What stops two recruiters overwriting each other on the board?

Every save carries the state the screen was showing when you started editing. If someone else
changed that candidate first, the save is refused and you are shown what changed instead of
quietly losing one of the two edits. This runs over ordinary REST requests, so it needs nothing
special on your server and works on any host that runs WordPress normally.

Is there a Pro version?

Yes. Vakanssi Pro is a separate plugin, coming soon, for teams that need more. Everything in this plugin stays free and fully working. Get notified when it launches at https://vakanssi.com/#notify
sections.changelog:
1.3.0

  • New: on multisite, a super admin sees the hiring data that deleted sites left behind (in Site Health, on the network Dashboard and Sites screens, and under Hiring → Tools → Status) and removes it under Hiring → Tools → Data after confirming. CV files that cannot be removed stay listed until you choose to stop tracking them.
  • Fixed: deleting a network site whose CVs could not all be deleted no longer loses the record of those files; Vakanssi keeps that site’s list of CV files so they can be found and removed later.
  • Fixed: a new network site that gets the ID of a deleted site no longer shows the deleted site’s candidates and applications as its own.
  • Fixed: on PHP 8, deleting a network site no longer stops with an error when a stored file name is damaged.

1.2.6

  • Fixed: a job page whose description contains the Job Details shortcode shows the details block once instead of twice.
  • Fixed: on themes that show an excerpt before the job description, the job page no longer loses its details block and apply form, and the excerpt no longer includes the job details.
  • Fixed: an apply form placed in the job description with its shortcode no longer disappears when an SEO plugin reads the page first.
  • Fixed: after a refused application, the candidate sees the reason instead of a generic error when another plugin reads the page before it is shown.
  • Fixed: while a stage move is still saving, the drawer no longer shows the candidate’s position in the new stage next to the old stage.
  • Fixed: on WordPress older than 6.7 with a block theme, the setup wizard no longer promises the branded job page layout, and a notice says job pages use your theme’s post layout until you update.
  • Fixed: an application whose CV is larger than the server’s upload limit goes back to the job page with the “too large” message instead of a blank page.
  • Fixed: very long interview locations, candidate names and candidate locations are shortened to fit. Before, saving could fail.
  • Fixed: the CSV job import no longer warns about a missing country for a row whose location was skipped.

1.2.5

  • Fixed: editing a location, even just its description, no longer changes the city of jobs in the locations under it, and editing “Remote” no longer gives remote jobs the city “Remote”.
  • Fixed: saving a job without changes keeps all of its locations, for example after an import, instead of keeping only the first one alphabetically.
  • Fixed: you can clear a job’s location, and a deleted location no longer comes back the next time a job is saved. Deleting a location also removes it as the city of the jobs that used it.
  • Changed: Quick Edit and Bulk Edit on All Jobs no longer offer locations, because they changed a job’s location without its city. Set the location in the job editor.
  • Fixed: a location or department name with no letters or numbers is skipped (the import log says so) instead of filing the job under an unrelated place or team.
  • Fixed: an “&” in a location now shows as “&” in Google for Jobs data, the REST API, job filters and the Jobs block, and location names over 200 characters save.
  • Fixed: changing a job’s city over the REST API also updates its location, and CSV import keeps backslashes in names, so importing the same file again finds the existing jobs.
  • Fixed: picking a team on the careers page also shows its sub-teams’ roles and roles that list it as a second team, matching the shortcode’s department setting.
  • Fixed: visitors can no longer list departments used only by draft, private, password-protected, expired or sample jobs through the REST API, or read department descriptions there.
  • Changed: the Departments and Locations screens explain each field in plain words, and saving jobs says “Job published” and “2 jobs updated” instead of “Post”.
